study: How 2026 legal-aid RFPs treat a vendor's own use of AI
frozen_note: Coding frozen before the grader was run. Calls were made by reading the collected text, by AI agents working in MV2's name; there is no second coder. Every call below has a verbatim quotation that the grader checks mechanically against the re-fetched source file.
coder_rules_applied: VENDOR_AI counts a sentence about what the bidder or contractor itself does with AI, or with the organisation's data in AI, while preparing the proposal or doing the work. Requirements on the AI system being delivered (for example 'the solution must not train on customer data') describe the product and are not VENDOR_AI; they are recorded as NOT_VENDOR_AI quotes and listed as borderline calls.

TECH means the vendor builds, configures, integrates or operates software, websites or systems, delivers IT services, or trains staff to build software. Work that only assesses, plans, evaluates, designs at concept level, sets governance or writes content is NON_TECH, even when the subject is a technology project.
AI_IN_SCOPE means the requested work itself includes AI the organisation wants or may want, including AI-generated outputs, AI tools to be governed, or groundwork for future AI.
Posted date: listing teaser, else the posting page, else the issue date printed in the document, else the upload-folder month (amendment 1).

Sensitivity frame (amendment 1): leaves out records found only by web_search_seed, and also does not use text that only a web_search_seed file supplied (so the LACI shared-governance posting, found by a listing capture but codable only through a seeded file, is not codable there). This reading was fixed before any count was computed.
